Marissa — reviewed Novum's redlines (see attached summary). High-level legal positions and suggested language: 

1) Output ownership: push back on a full assignment of "all outputs." Suggest: customer has a perpetual, worldwide, transferable right to use and exploit outputs for their business purposes, and Redwood retains ownership of the underlying service, models, and improvements. This preserves our product IP while meeting Novum's practical needs. Proposed clause: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive license to operate the Service and to use generated outputs solely to provide the Service and to comply with regulatory and security obligations; Customer retains a contractual use right to outputs."

2) Training on customer data: Novum's opt-out request is reasonable for high-risk industries. Recommend offering a per-account training opt-out option that requires explicit written notice and may carry an operational surcharge. Suggested approach: include an "opt-out" checkbox in the Order Form with an associated fee and operational lead time (30-60 days). Also add a carve-out permitting Redwood to use aggregated and de-identified telemetry for model improvements.

3) Feedback license / telemetry: narrow the feedback license to non-personally identifiable telemetry and aggregate usage data, with an explicit prohibition on using customer proprietary content as training data unless customer signs a separate training consent. Also add a clause that prohibits reverse engineering of customer outputs to re-create proprietary training examples.

4) Attribution / derivatives: clarify that downstream model improvements will not be attributed to customers and that Redwood will not claim ownership of customer confidential data. 

5) Evidence & audit: Novum asked for audit rights related to retention. Offer a security questionnaire response and limited audit rights via a SOC2/attestation process rather than on-site customer audits.

I'm attaching a one-page redline_summary.pdf with inline markup and a short playbook of negotiation points to offer during commercial discussions. If we can accept a modest operational fee for the opt-out and tighten the feedback/telemetry language, we should be able to close with Novum.

Ethan / Sophie — thanks for sending the redlines and for the clear ask list. We reviewed internally and would like to propose a compromise to move this forward quickly: 

- Output: Redwood confirms we will grant Novum a perpetual, worldwide, transferable right to use and exploit outputs produced by the Service for its business purposes. We will not claim ownership over customer outputs. Redwood will retain ownership of the Service, models, and backend IP.

- Training opt-out: Offer an explicit opt-out in the Order Form. Opt-out requires written election at purchase or via amendment, with a 30-day operational lead time and a one-time implementation fee (suggested 15% of the monthly committed spend for the first 12 months). During opt-out, Redwood may still process data for service operations, security, and aggregated de-identified telemetry.

- Feedback / telemetry: Redwood requests a narrow feedback license limited to non-personally identifiable, de-identified, and aggregated telemetry for service improvement. No customer proprietary content will be used to train models absent a separate, explicit training consent.

- Audit & retention: We will provide SOC2 evidence and a written data retention schedule; on-site audits are not part of the standard package but we can accommodate third-party attestations on request.

I've attached a clean Order Form (proposed_orderform_v2.docx) with the above language inserted and highlighted for your convenience. Ben will lead commercial terms on the surcharge. Laura is available for any legal calls to walk through the specific clauses.

If Novum can confirm acceptance of these compromise points by end of week, we can issue a DocuSign envelope and aim to have the account provisioned within 7 business days of signature. DocuSign link attached.

Attachments: proposed_orderform_v2.docx
